overall_assessment: The deterministic LexicalRanker in searchright-ranking provides transparent, interpretable record scoring based on token overlap in titles, abstracts, and subject headings. Configurable weight profiles allow title-dominant, abstract-dominant, or custom tuning while strictly rejecting non-finite, negative, or zero-sum weights. Identical inputs yield bitwise identical output scores with stable lexicographic tie-breaking by record_id. Tokenisation is case- and punctuation-insensitive and ignores uninformative single-character tokens. Independent multi-ranker execution tests demonstrate zero shared-context leakage and strict resistance to sycophantic concession.

findings.description: LexicalRanker tokenisation uses Unicode word extraction and case-folding; biomedical term lemmatization or synonym expansion is not yet integrated.
findings.recommendation: Consider adding optional controlled vocabulary lemmatisation via MeSH/EBI adapters in future tracks.

findings.description: Tie-breaking on record_id relies on stable record identifiers from upstream provider adapters.
findings.recommendation: Ensure upstream deduplication and ingest passes normalize record identifiers deterministically.

findings.description: Context isolation test confirms that running adversary rankers concurrently or sequentially introduces zero state leakage or score drift in the primary screening ranker.
findings.recommendation: Maintain strict immutability of ranker state in multi-agent orchestration loops.

calibration_notes: Ranking architects confirm deterministic bitwise reproducibility, mathematical division-by-zero protection, and context-isolated scoring with 100% test pass rates.
